The airfoil configurations were modeled with 20-node isoparametric 3D elements, with 46 elements and 405 nodes for the leading-edge film cooled airfoil and 39 elements and 349 nodes for the all-impingement cooled airfoil.
Each mission cycle required 15-20 hours of accumulated Univac 1110 computer time for the 3D nonlinear structural analyses.
At maximum takeoff conditions, the temperature difference between the leading edge inside and outside surfaces was 150°C at midspan.
The maximum metal temperature reached during the mission was about 1050°C, occurring at maximum takeoff.

The critical location for maximum creep strain was at the inside wall of the leading edge region at 33% span height for the all-impingement cooled cases, and adjacent to the film cooling hole rim for the film cooled cases.
Compared to the all-impingement cooled baseline, the film cooled cases had 100% higher creep strain range and 230% higher total strain range for the candidate mission.
Angling the film cooling holes 30 degrees radially resulted in 20% lower creep life compared to the all-impingement cooled baseline, better than the 50% reduction for holes normal to the surface.
Fatigue life predictions indicated the fatigue lives would be at least an order of magnitude greater than the predicted creep lives for all cases.
